predecessors.name: Northern Wei
predecessors.text: the western part of the Northern Wei: Guanzhong and Gansu under Yuwen Tai

successors.name: Northern Zhou
successors.text: the whole Western Wei realm, handed to Yuwen Jue in 557

ledger.x: 534: the Northern Wei splits and Yuwen Tai rules the west.
537: Yuwen Tai attacks the Eastern Wei.
537: the Western Wei hold the Luoyang region.
538: the Western Wei leave the Luoyang region.
543: the Western Wei are driven off again.
553: Hanzhong goes to the Western Wei.
555: the Western Liang is set up at Jiangling.
557: the Western Liang passes to the Northern Zhou with the Western Wei's fall (the puppet-state line lists the Northern Zhou next).

wars.name: Eastern Wei-Western Wei wars
wars.outcome: No lasting change of frontier on the pages opened: Hengnong taken in fall 537, Hulao surrendered in spring 543, Gao Huan's attack on Yubi in 546; the Eastern Wei ended in 550.

wars.name: Western Wei conquest of the western Liang
wars.outcome: Western Wei took Xiangyang (549), Sichuan (spring 553) and Jiangling (winter 554), killed Emperor Yuan and set up the puppet Western Liang under Xiao Cha in 555.

certainty.note: The Eastern Wei frontier moved by campaign at Hengnong and Hulao; the Rouran, Tuyuhun and Tujue frontiers are approximate, and no treaty or survey fixes any edge.
